author: Dawkes
asr_identification: the medieval citadel of Taraz under the central market of modern Taraz (formerly Dzhambul/Aulie-ata), Zhambyl province, Kazakhstan
evidence: UCL–Kazakh excavation 2011–12 (c. 400 m²) in the central market, within the former citadel: the earliest structures are two superposed mudbrick walls, possibly the citadel circuit, tentatively 7th–8th c.; above them four buildings of the 9th–12th c. (domestic flame shrine, workshop, shops; stone building; hamam with a C14 date in the late 12th c., SUERC-38682); no occupation after c. 1200. Earliest written mention of the city 568 (Byzantine embassy).
quote: The earliest structure identified in the excavation consisted of truncated portions of mudbrick walls in the north-west corner of the site, possibly representing parts of the citadel circuit, tentatively dated to the 7th to 8th centuries … clearly demonstrated the abundance of stratified archaeological deposits of the medieval citadel that survive under the area of the modern market-place
note: Agrees with Mizutani and the study (Bernshtam's excavations, via Ji): new excavation confirms the medieval city under modern Taraz, with a citadel wall perhaps of Xuanzang's time; the 7th–8th c. date is tentative, and the article does not mention Xuanzang.

author: Yamauchi et al.
name_in_asr: アク・ベシム（スイヤブ）遺跡
asr_identification: Ak-Beshim, Chu valley, N Kyrgyzstan: Shahristan 1 the walled town; Shahristan 2 (formerly the 'Rabat' or Karakhitai quarter) = the Tang garrison town 砕葉鎮城
evidence: Excavations 2015–17 in Shahristan 1 (a N–S street lined with metal workshops and houses with bread ovens) and Shahristan 2, with geophysical survey; Shahristan 2, previously taken for an 11th–12th c. suburb, shown by excavation to be the Tang Suiye garrison (westernmost of the Anxi Four Garrisons); the Usman canal, taken off the Chu upstream, watered the town and its fields; Sogdian ink inscriptions on finds being read; textual study of 素葉 in the Xiyu ji and the Life.
quote: 発掘調査の結果、この街が中国史書に記載された「砕葉鎮城」であることが明らかとなった。…これまでもアク・ベシム遺跡がスイヤブ、そして砕葉鎮であったと推測されてきたが、発掘調査によってそれを確定することができたのは大きな成果である。
note: Agrees with the study (Ak-Beshim = Suyab, high) and adds excavation: the Tang Suiye fort (built 679, after Xuanzang) is fixed in Shahristan 2, so by implication the town Xuanzang saw in 630 is Shahristan 1, the Sogdian city. A summary report; the detailed reports are Jokura et al. 2016, 2017 and Yamauchi et al. 2018.

author: Kolchenko
asr_identification: the Ak-Beshim settlement, Chu valley, Kyrgyzstan
evidence: All excavated Buddhist buildings of the Chu valley (Ak-Beshim AB-0, AB-1, AB-2; Krasnaya Rechka KrR-1–3) and the Buddhist steles and bronzes date after Xuanzang: Buddhism came with the Tang garrison (city wall of 679, Dayun temples ordered 692–705); Xuanzang's record and the Life say nothing of Buddhism at Suyab in 629/30. Kolchenko takes the 679 wall for the wall round Shahristan 2 (Chinese-type tiles inside it) and argues that AB-0, inside Shahristan 2, not AB-1 (Clauson), was the Dayun-si.
quote: Chinese monk Xuanzang (629 / 630) who stayed at Suyab, the capital of the Western Turkic Khaganate, which was identified as the local city at the Ak-Beshim settlement. In his notes, Xuanzang says nothing about Buddhism in Suyab … this castle wall should be identified with the wall around Shakhristan-2
note: Agrees (Ak-Beshim = Suyab). Adds a consistency check from the excavator: the Xiyu ji reports no Buddhism at 素葉水城, and the Buddhist remains at Ak-Beshim are all Tang or later; the Tang fort is placed in Shahristan 2, leaving Shahristan 1 as the town of 630.

author: Tarzi
name_in_asr: the “Eastern” monastery with the 1000-foot reclining Buddha
asr_identification: the 'Eastern' monastery at the foot of the E part of the Buddha cliff, SE of the 38 m Buddha, near the only Bamiyan stupa (square M), Bamiyan valley, Afghanistan
evidence: French mission 2002–03: trenches on a 5 m grid, 3.5–5.6 m deep, along the E side of the large square M (100 × 80 m), round the stupa and E of the square; in sounding A9 a mass of clay mouldings fallen from a monument with seven heads/masks of Buddhist divinities; round the stupa three rooms paved with limestone or schist, burnt (perhaps 9th c.), Ghaznavid and Ghurid sherds. No coin or ceramic date for the foundation (perhaps as early as the 3rd c.); the reclining image itself not found.
quote: The “Eastern” monastery is located to the southeast of the 38-meter standing Buddha statue, somewhere in the lower area of the eastern part of the great cliff and not far from the only Bamiyan … This discovery confirms that the excavators have discovered the Bamiyan ”Eastern” monastery visited by Xuanzang where the 1000-foot-long reclining Buddha statue may yet be found.
note: Not in the notes. A third placing, close to Foucher's eastern alternative: Tarzi seeks the reclining-Buddha monastery below the E end of the cliff, SE of the 38 m Buddha, not between the two colossi (Kuwayama). He has excavated a Buddhist monastery there but no reclining image, so the attribution is his assumption, not proof; 01.37.02 stays open (Mizutani: not identified). Later Tarzi seasons (from 2004) would be needed to judge it.

author: Talati (娃斯玛·塔拉提)
asr_identification: the Khotan royal city, unmoved from Han to Tang, in the centre of the oasis between the Yurung-kash and Kara-kash; Yotkan only its E or SE part, the core further W (Khotan county, Xinjiang)
evidence: No fieldwork: Yotkan has never been scientifically excavated (gold-washing from the late 1860s left a pit 8–9 m deep). Argument from texts and murals: Northern-dynasty histories give the capital 8–9 li round (c. 3.7–4.8 km); Tibetan texts (Li yul lung bstan pa, Li yul chos kyi lo rgyus) name a N gate with gate tower, a S gate, a N street, the 7-storey Vaiśravaṇa temple by the N gate, a great bazaar and the 'sea-eye' temple, and put the 'sea-eye' at the centre of the land of Khotan and inside the royal city; Mogao cave 454 (early Song) paints a square walled city between two rivers below a mountain; Gao Juhui (938) has the palaces facing E, so the palace quarter lay W of the main N–S street.
quote: 笔者尝试用新的研究方法重新论证，认为于阗王城在汉唐时期并未发生过变迁，约特干遗址只是于阗王城的东或东南部分，而王城的核心区则在更西处。…这就表明，于阗王城位于于阗地方的正中，亦即今和田绿洲的中心位置。
note: Agrees that Yotkan belongs to the royal city (study: Yotkan, high) but places the core W of Yotkan, without site evidence. If right, the 王城 from which Xuanzang measures (Somiya 5–6 li W, Kum-i-Shahidān SE, Bowa-Kambar SW) lies a little W of Stein's centre; the existing distance fit is not tested in the paper.

author: Talati (娃斯玛·塔拉提)
asr_identification: reviews: Ilchi (Qing); Yotkan (Grenard, Stein); Yotkan for Wei and Five Dynasties with the Tang capital in the mountains S of the oasis (Shirai 1933); Ak-sipil, then Shisbir = Melikawat (Huang Wenbi); the Naghara-khana mound and Alalbagh village E of Yotkan (Yin Qing 1983, Li Yinping 1989); the royal palace at Birga (Birgaṃdara) in the Domoko river area of Chira (Duan Qing 2013; Rong & Zhu 2013)
evidence: Survey of earlier proposals; the 'Birga' palace thesis rests on Khotanese documents excavated at Khotan.
quote: 格热纳德（F. Grenard）、斯坦因（M. A. Stein）率先指出，…和田绿洲中的约特干遗址是于阗王城故址…约特干可能是魏和五代时期的王城遗址，唐代王城则在和田绿洲以南的山中…殷晴、李吟屏提出新的假说，将约特干遗址以东不远处的奈加拉·哈奈 土墩、阿拉勒巴…格村比定为于阗王城故址…推断策勒达玛沟河流域的“拔伽”…（Birga dara）才是于阗王宫所在地
note: The notes give only Huang Wenbi's Shisbir as a rival (via Ji). Further alternatives: Shirai's Tang capital in the southern mountains; Yin Qing/Li Yinping's Naghara-khana mound (which the study takes for the 龍鼓池側伽藍, 12.22.10); and the Birga palace in Domoko. Zhang 2016 (this batch) identifies Birgaṃdara with Balawaste, a Six-Towns site under Cira, which tells against a royal seat there. Talati herself keeps Yotkan; none of these displaces it.

author: Zhang
name_in_asr: Phema; Khot. phęmāña kīṃtha 'the Fort of Phema'; Chin. 坎城; Tib. Kam sheng
asr_identification: the old fort Kanaqin (卡那沁) by Ulugh-Ziārat, c. 3 miles SE of Uzun-Tati, N of Chira (Qira), Xinjiang (after Li Yinping 1998)
evidence: Bilingual Hedin 24: Khot. phęmāña kīṃtha corresponds to Chin. 坎城 (Tib. Kam sheng); Huang Wenbi (1958) recorded the fort's local name as Kanaqin, which Li Yinping (1998) explains as a rendering of 坎城; under the Tang a small 守捉 garrison sat there, and the Tibetans kept it as their military seat in the Cira–Six Towns prefecture; Archive 3 orders (c. 798) were issued 'here in Phema, in the fort' by the prefect Sudārrjāṃ and Blon Rmang-bzher. Phema lay in the prefecture but was not one of the Six Towns.
quote: phęmāña kīṃtha corresponds to Kǎnchéng 坎城 ‘the fort of Kan’. … Phema, on the other hand, corresponds to Chin. Pìmó 媲摩 in Xuan Zang’s Xiyuji … Especially noteworthy is the old fort that Stein (1907, p.462) visited and examined in the vicinity of Ulūgh-Ziārat … Li Yinping (1998, pp.255-262) convincingly identified this fort with Kǎnchéng 坎城
note: Adds evidence. Ji already has Hedin 24 making 媲摩 = 坎城; new is the tie of 坎城/Phema to one ruin, the Kanaqin fort by Ulugh-Ziārat, through its modern name. That favours Ulugh-Ziārat over Uzun-Tati for 媲摩, i.e. Mizutani's allocation rather than Stein's, though Zhang still cites Stein's Uzun-Tati and does not discuss the question. The name argument is Li Yinping's (1998), not checked here. The area stands.

author: Zhang
name_in_asr: Pimo (with Song Yun's Hanmo, Marco Polo's Pein)
asr_identification: Ulūgh Mazar (Stein's identification), N of the Domoko–Chira area
evidence: Stein's coin finds on his revisit (second expedition, 1908): Wuzhu (5th c.), a Sino-Kharoṣṭhī coin, Tang coins (7th–8th c.), Song coins (12th c.) and a 14th-c. Islamic coin, so occupation ran from before 519 through the Tang to the Karakhanid period.
quote: These numismatic finds demonstrate that Ulūgh Mazar was continuously occupied from a period before Song Yun’s visit to Khotan in 519, through the entire Tang period, until the Kharakhanid period, if not later. Stein also confirmed his identification of this site with Hanmo in Song Yun’s account, Pimo in Xuanzang’s account
note: Reports Stein's own evidence: occupation spans Xuanzang's date. Zhang's summary attaches Hanmo, Pimo and Pein all to one site (Ulūgh Mazar), unlike the Uzun-Tati/Ulugh-Ziārat split in the note; which ruin Zhang means should be checked against Serindia before it is used.

author: Zhang
evidence: Li yul lung bstan pa: a monastery Bhavanya built by the king of Khotan while Mgar Btsan nyen controlled Khotan (687–692), identified (by others, his n. 280) with Xuanzang's Dīrghabhavana.
quote: the King of Khotan built a monastery called Bhavanya, identified with the Dīrghabhavana Monastery mentioned by Xuan Zang.
note: No location. If the identification holds, the Tibetan legend dates the foundation some 45 years after Xuanzang's visit (644), so either the identification or the legend's date is wrong; no bearing on Bowa-Kambar.

author: Mock
evidence: Field record of Old Tibetan inscriptions, mchod rten drawings and rock art along the Afghan Wakhan route; the Tang campaign of 747 against the Tibetan fort of Lien-yün near Sarhad-e Broghil; Stein's visit to the Kansir fort above Korkut (S bank).
note: 8th-c. Tibetan–Tang context for Wakhan; Xuanzang is not mentioned and Khandūd (12.15.02) is not discussed.

author: Stančo et al.
asr_identification: the Darband Wall across the Shurob valley between Sarymas and Susiztag, Baysun district, Surxondaryo, Uzbekistan
evidence: Ten radiocarbon dates from a section of the wall: first phase in the first half/middle of the 3rd c. BC, rebuilt with mudbrick under the Kushans (1st–2nd c. AD); Hellenistic coins (61 of the 3rd–2nd c. BC) from surface collections 2018–22.
note: An ancient barrier on the Bactria–Sogdiana road near Derbent, distinct from the Buzgala defile the study takes for 鐵門; the article does not discuss Xuanzang or a 7th-c. phase; no bearing on 01.20.01.

author: Kuwayama
name_in_asr: 佛入涅槃臥像 / 臥像伽藍 (先王伽藍)
asr_identification: a vanished monastery built by the 先王, between the West (55 m) and East (38 m) Buddhas at Bamiyan, Afghanistan; the reclining image was of clay
evidence: Text, not site: the Life says the reclining image is inside (伽藍內) the monastery E of the West Buddha, while no building is named for the standing images; Daoxuan's 釋迦方志 writes 涅槃臥素佛 (素 = 塑, clay). Comparanda: clay reclining Buddhas housed in buildings at Tapa Sardar (Ghazni), restored length c. 15 m, and Adjina Tepa (Tajikistan), c. 21 m. Nothing survives of the Bamiyan monastery or image.
quote: 臥像伽藍は東西二.大俳の中間にあった｡臥像については伽藍内と言い'立俳については伽藍の存在を言わない … 道宣はこれを現行の﹃西域記﹄にはみえない｢素｣を入れて'｢浬薬臥素併｣につ‑っている … 復原長は前者が一五メ1‑ル'後者が二一メ1‑ルを測る長大な塑像である
note: First publication of the argument the notes already give from Kuwayama 1990 (pp. 1436–53) and 2002 (p. 154); nothing new except the restored lengths of the Tapa Sardar (c. 15 m) and Adjina Tepa (c. 21 m) comparanda. Agrees with the study's preferred alternative (Kuwayama's middle monastery, low confidence); Mizutani gives no site.

author: Kuwayama
name_in_asr: (route) バーミヤーン–シバル峠–ゴルバンド河流域–カーピシー
asr_identification: the Shibar pass and the Ghorband valley as the normal road from Bamiyan to Kapisi, Afghanistan
evidence: General statement on the route, not on Xuanzang's crossing: the trunk road from the Ghorband over the Shibar pass to the Surkhab valley was in long use until the Salang highway opened in 1964; in the 6th century a traveller from the Hephthalite winter camp would have gone up the Surkhab to Bamiyan, over the Shibar to the Ghorband and on to Kapisi.
quote: バー､､､ヤーンからシバル峠をこえてゴルバンド河流域に出'カーピシーからナガラハ‑ラへと進めたはずである … 従来永‑使われたゴルバンドからシ一パル峠をこえてスルハーブ流 … 域に出る幹線道路が至るところで通行の困難をきたすことになった
note: Not in the notes for 01.37.03a. Like Foucher, Kuwayama treats the Shibar–Ghorband road as the highway; he does not discuss the crossing after the detour to 01.37.03, so it does not decide between Mizutani's Shibar and the study's leaning to Hajigak/Unai.

author: Kuwayama
asr_identification: Khandud (Khandūd), S bank of the Ab-i Panja, Wakhan, Afghanistan; royal town of 達摩悉鐵帝 in Xuanzang's time
evidence: Text: Wakhan (鉢和/護密, Xuanzang's 達摩悉鐵帝, Dharmagupta's 達摩悉嚢多) had two main settlements, 昏馱多 and 塞迦審; 昏馱多 was the royal town when Xuanzang passed; the centre later moved to 塞迦審, which the Tang shu gives as the chief settlement, probably Ishkashim WSW of Khandud where the Ab-i Panja bends north. No site evidence.
quote: 昏駄多と塞迦審の二大集落があり'玄突通過時には昏駄多が王城であった｡これは今のバンドウードと考えられてワッハーンを西流するア‑ベ=パンジャの南岸にあり'おそらく塞迦審へその後中心を移し'﹃唐書﹄には塞迦審が主たる集落と記されるに至ったのである｡これは今のイシュカーシムらしく
note: Agrees with Mizutani and the study (Khandud); not in the notes. Adds that the Wakhan seat moved later to 塞迦審 = Ishkashim (see 12.16a).

author: Kuwayama
asr_identification: 塞迦審 = Ishkashim, the later chief town of Wakhan (護密), not of Shighnan
evidence: Text: the Tang shu's 塞迦審 is the later chief settlement of Wakhan (護密), to which the centre moved from 昏馱多; probably Ishkashim at the bend of the Ab-i Panja, the W entrance of Wakhan towards Zebak over the Sardab pass.
quote: おそらく塞迦審へその後中心を移し'﹃唐書﹄には塞迦審が主たる集落と記されるに至ったのである｡これは今のイシュカーシムらしく
note: Implicit: Kuwayama does not discuss Shighnan, but by putting 塞迦審/Ishkashim in Wakhan he removes the Tang-shu name on which Mizutani's tentative 'perhaps Ishkashim (= 塞迦審城)' for the Shighnan capital rests. The study already calls 12.16a open; this weakens the Ishkashim suggestion further.

author: Kuwayama
asr_identification: Begram (Begram III), Parwan, Afghanistan, still occupied in the 7th century
evidence: Dating of Begram III to the 7th c. against Ghirshman's end c. 400: round bastions and stamped (円圏押印紋) pottery appear together at Begram III and Tapa Skandar II by the 7th c. at the latest; the small fort of Kohna Masjid in Baghlan, N of the Hindu Kush, has round bastions and southern-type stamped pottery and, placed in the Baghlan–Kunduz pottery sequence, dates to the 6th–7th c. (the excavator's Varahran IV coin gave 5th c.). Text: the three 舊王 monasteries are on the S bank of the Panjshir NW of the city without distances, so the city lay close to the river, excluding Ghirshman's Gunde Paisa 5 km S (c. 10 li).
quote: 問題は（8）と（9）と（10）である。大河南岸で，王都城の北西，そこに旧王伽藍があり，その南東にもうひとつ別の旧王伽藍がある。さらに後者の南東に旧王妃伽藍がある。ここにみえる大河がいまのパンジュシーール河であることは疑いない。この三伽藍以外はみな里数で示されている。しかもパンジュシール河の南岸にあるのであれば，王都城の遺跡としてベグラームのほかに候補としてあがるものはない。 … 北側のバグラーンにあるコフナ・マスジドKohnaMaslidの名でよばれる小城塞は，二二の伝統ともいうべき方形稜墨に加えて，北側ではたえて存在しなかった円形二丁を導入している。 … ベグラーム第皿期の年代はGhirshmanが考えたよりはるかに後までさがる。すなわち7世紀にベグラームは生きていたのである
note: Same conclusion and the Gunde Paisa argument as in the notes (Kuwayama 1990, pp. 736–50; 2002, chs. X–XI); this article gives the dating chain in more detail, notably the Kohna Masjid cross-date from N of the Hindu Kush. Agrees with Mizutani and the study (Begram).

author: Kuwayama
asr_identification: Shotorak, N foot of Koh-i Pahlawan, E of Begram, Parwan, Afghanistan (dated; not linked here to the 質子伽藍)
evidence: Site dating: Shotorak yielded stamped pottery so close to that of Tapa Skandar II that the same stamps may have been used (also shared with Tapa Sardar and Gul Dara), and round bastions on obtuse-angled walls; its main stupa was rebuilt at least once and schist sculpture reused as building stone. Kuwayama concludes Shotorak shared the 7th–8th c. with Tapa Skandar II, i.e. it was in use in Xuanzang's time.
quote: ベグラーム東方，ショトラクのプランは異常であり，比較の対象を欠く。 … この佛寺とタパ＝シカンダルとを時期の点で結び附けるのは，隅じ施紋具を使ったのではないかと思わせるほどに類同した円圏押印紋の土器片を出土していることであり … したがってこの寺もまたタパ・シカンダルと7ないし8世紀を共有していたはずである。
note: Not in the notes: the notes have Kuwayama (1990, 2002) choosing no ruin on the hill. This dates one candidate (Shotorak) to the 7th–8th c., so it could be the monastery Xuanzang saw, but it does not tie Shotorak to the 質子伽藍 and does not touch the study's preference for Foucher's ruin on the S spur (北山下). Agrees with Mizutani's hill.

author: Kuwayama
note: Dates the Kabul Turk kings from the Gardez Gaṇeśa inscription and separates the Kāpiśī Khingal dynasty (Kṣatriya, per Xiyu ji 1) from the Hephthalite Khiṅgila; no Xiyu ji place is located. The one locational remark (Udabhāṇḍapura as Kāpiśī's eastern capital, pp. 30–31) is already in the notes from Kuwayama 2002, p. 210 (02.04.18).

author: Kuwayama
asr_identification: Kāpiśī: the Xiyu ji's country = the limited area round Begram, E of Charikar; the Khingal king's dominion reached E through Gandhāra to the W bank of the Indus, SE to Bannu, S to Kabul
evidence: Textual: the Xiyu ji (juan 11) makes 伐剌拏 (Bannu) subject to Kāpiśī; the Life has Xuanzang go with the Kāpiśī king from Udabhāṇḍa, Kāpiśī's eastern border town, to Lampāka, 伐剌拏, 阿薄健 and 漕矩吒; Tang records give the dynasty's founder 馨孽 (*Khingal), 12 generations to 653/658.
quote: 『大唐西域記』に記述された迦畢試園はアフガニスタン東部,Charikar東方にあるBegr豆m道連を中心とする限定された範囲であるが,支配地域は西はこのBegr豆m一帯の地域,東は膏のGandharaでインダス河西岸まで,東南はGandh豆raの南,いまのパキスタンのBannu地方におよび … 『大唐西域記』金11に伐刺挙国が迦畢試園に役属しているとある
note: Agrees with Mizutani's Begram-centred Kāpiśī. New against the notes: the distinction between the country Xuanzang describes (the Begram basin) and the king's wider dominion (to the Indus, Bannu and Kabul), which bears on the notes' remark that the authorities differ on Kāpiśī's extent. The summer/winter capitals (Begram/Udabhāṇḍapura) are already in the notes from Kuwayama 2002, p. 210.

author: Kuwayama
asr_identification: a large district centred on Kabul, reaching SW to Wardak and E to the Kotal-e Lataband; much nearer Kāpiśī than Ghazni
evidence: Textual and distance argument: the Life puts the country 500 li N of 漕矩吒 and has Xuanzang go from it NE over mountains past some tens of Kāpiśī border towns to the Khawak; Begram–Kabul c. 70 km, Kabul–Ghazni c. 150 km; its size (2000 × 1000 li) exceeds Kāpiśī's 4000 li circuit. 阿路猱山 (Khair Khana) lies at Kabul's N edge, so the country is almost Kāpiśī's southern frontier.
quote: このことは弗乗侍薩償郡がKapi畠Ll‑Ghazni間にあるものの,Ghazn王よりはるかに遠く,K瓦pi畠iにより近接していることを示すものであろう … 中心はK豆bul,西南はWardak,東はKota1‑eLatabandに及ぶ虞大な地域である … 阿路狭山はK豆pi畠iの両界にも位置していた｡つまり弗実情薩償那(K豆bul)はほとんど迦畢試の南彊である
note: Same identification as Kuwayama 2002, p. 198 (already in the note); more detailed here: the Life's route NE through the Kāpiśī border towns and the measured distances, which make the country adjoin Kāpiśī rather than Zābulistān. Supports the study's Kabul reading (with Wardak) against the Koh-daman; differs from Mizutani only in giving a centre where he leaves the location open.

author: Kuwayama
asr_identification: the Khawak pass of the Hindu Kush, between Andarāb and the Panjshir valley
evidence: Route: the Life's 越迦畢試國邊城小邑凡數十所至大雪山婆羅犀那大嶺 glossed as the Khawak; Begram lies on the N–S route from Andarāb over the Khawak down the Panjshir to its Ghorband confluence, the route by which the Kāpiśī king escorted Xuanzang back to Tokharistan.
quote: K豆pi畠i園の連蓮のまちやむらおよそ数十所を経過して,Hindukush山脈のKhawak峠に至る … Khawak峠を越えてPanjshir河をくだり,Ghorband河と合流する地艶こ位置す多という南北交通の要衝にあり,K豆pi畠主王に護透された
note: Agrees with Mizutani and the note (Khawak); Kuwayama is not yet cited there (also Kuwayama 2002, p. 132; 1999, p. 60). Adds no field evidence, only the Panjshir approach from Begram, as Foucher.

author: Kuwayama
note: This is the article the notes cite as 'Kuwayama 2000' (Zinbun 34(1), pp. 25–77): Borj-e Kafir (p. 26), Tapa Skandar = 霫蔽多伐剌祠 (p. 27), Mount Aruṇa = Khair Khana and 䅳那 = Sui 順 (pp. 27–36), Sui 漕 = Kāpiśī (pp. 30–32), 弗栗恃薩儻那 = Kabul to Wardak and the Lataband (p. 57). Its chapters reappear in Kuwayama 2002 (chs. XII–XV). Nothing locational beyond what the notes have; the citation year in the notes should read 1999.

author: Kuwayama
asr_identification: Tokhāra as Xuanzang lists it: 8 territories N of the Amu (Termez to Kumedh) and 21 S of it, 29 in all; without the three W of Balkh (鋭秣陀, 胡寔健, 呾剌健) 26, near the 24 (or 25) 州 of the Tang 月氏都督府
evidence: Count of the Xiyu ji's own list against the Tang commandery lists (Jiu Tangshu 40, Xin Tangshu 221下, Tang huiyao 99); the Ḥudūd's Tokharistan lies only E of Khulm (Surkhāb basin and beyond), Balkh and Khulm excluded
quote: よって南岸は 21 地方で，「往昔のトハーラ地方」は総数 29 地方から成り立っていた。…縛喝以西，西南にある 3 地方，鋭秣陀，胡寔健，呾剌健は，ヒンドゥークシュの北部にありといわれるトハーラからは外れている。従ってこれを除くと 26 国。
note: New to the notes: Kuwayama's tally of 29 (Ji's 29 states is a bare count) and his exclusion of the three western countries, which differs from Miyamoto 2015 (Gūzgān included as Bactrian-speaking). The region itself is unaffected; Mizutani stands.

author: Kuwayama
asr_identification: Route: from the Iron Gate (Derbent) down the Surkhan Darya to Termez; the Life's route crosses the Amu and reaches 活 'several hundred li' on, probably by boat
evidence: Reading of 順縛芻河北下流至呾蜜國 (correcting his own 1987 translation and Mizutani's 'to the country of Tokhāra' for 故地); no field evidence
quote: 「縛芻河の北方にいき，それからスルハーンダリヤ (Surkhan Darya) を下ってテ…『慈恩伝』はテルメズに言及せず，鉄門をこえてから縛芻河を渡って数百里で活国に至ったとする。これが実際の旅程であって，舟運によったのであ
note: Text reading only; agrees with Termez (01.21). The river crossing to 活 by boat fits a capital on the Amu bank (Qal'a-ye Zāl), the study's working point for 12.05, but is Kuwayama's inference. Not in the notes.

author: Kuwayama
asr_identification: Barig (gloss only; no site given)
evidence: None; a bare gloss in his list of the S-bank territories
quote: 鉢 利 曷 (Barig)，訖 栗 瑟 摩 (Kishm)
note: Differs: the notes have only Parghar (Markwart, Ji) and Farkhar; Kuwayama's 'Barig' is unargued and unlocated, so it does not move the place, which stays unidentified. Worth checking against Kuwayama 1987 (translation notes).

author: Kuwayama
asr_identification: Munjān (gloss only)
evidence: None; a bare gloss
quote: 阿 利 尼 (Alini)，瞢 健 (Munjān)，活 (War)
note: Differs from his own 2002 'modern Talaqan' (notes, 12.06) in wording only: Munjān is the name, which the notes already accept; no site argued. The study's Taliqan–Khanabad working point is unaffected.

author: Kuwayama
asr_identification: pre-10th-century Khulm probably N of the present town (Tashkurghan)
evidence: Surface impression from walks round Khulm in 1963, 1974, 1977, 1978; Aramaic documents of the 4th c. BC name Khulm as a station of the satrap's governor (Naveh & Shaked 2012, pp. 19-20, 99)
quote: 1963，1974，1977，1978 年とフルム近辺を歩いてみた様子では，…いまのフルムより北側に 10 世紀以前のフルムは多分あったと思う。
note: Adds: agrees with Mizutani's ruins N of Tashkurgan from Kuwayama's own visits; the Aramaic mention of Khulm is new to the notes. No excavation.

author: Kuwayama
asr_identification: the large town site N of Qal'a-ye Zāl; Khesht Tepe to the W (findspot of the Kunduz hoard) is somewhat smaller
evidence: Site size comparison (Le Berre 1965 for Khesht Tepe); a site close to the S bank of the Amu is essential
quote: それより西の，いわゆるクンドゥズ遺宝を得たへシュトテペ (Khesht Tepe) は少し規模がちいさい［Le Berre 1965 : 83-88］。いずれにせよ，遺跡がアム河南岸に接近して立地することが同定には肝要である。
note: The Qal'a-ye Zāl argument, the Kyoto sherds and the Bālā Ḥiṣār trench are already in the notes (12.05); only the Khesht Tepe comparison is new: a second S-bank candidate, set aside by Kuwayama on size.

author: Miyamoto
asr_identification: Tokharistan in Xuanzang's sense = the Bactrian-speaking area, so its W limit includes Gūzgān W of Balkh
evidence: Xuanzang's note on the 25-letter script read left to right is Bactrian; Bactrian documents written in Gūzgān (Sims-Williams 2004, 2005); Iwai's ceramics show N and S of the Amu as one area 3rd-8th c.
quote: 筆者は，玄奘がバクトリア語の使用されていた地域をトハーリスターンとみなしたのではないかと推測している。…この推測が成り立つとすれば，バルフ以西，グーズガーン辺りまでの地域をトハーリスターンに含めて考えることが可能となる。
note: New to the notes; agrees with Mizutani's wide region (to Persia in the W) and differs from Kuwayama 1987/2020, who puts the W limit near Balkh.

author: Miyamoto
asr_identification: the domain of the khār of Rob: Samingan (N) to Madr and Kahmard (S), along the Khulm river
evidence: Bactrian docs N and Q (court and market of the khār of Rob in the district of Samingan), J, U (Madr), V (Kah, Rizm); the Tang 遲散州 set at 悉蜜言城 = Samingan (Chavannes)
quote: この Rob の khār の支配領域を漢文資料の中に探ると，玄奘が覩貨邏の二十七国の 1 つとして挙げる「紇露悉泯健」国が，それとほぼ合致しそうである。…玄奘は在地の支配者が実際に統治していた領域を「国」と呼んでいたことが分かるのである。…遲 散 州 が 置 か れ た 悉 蜜 言 城 で あ り
note: The notes (01.30, Name) make the same argument from BDNA without crediting Miyamoto, who made it in 2015; he adds the southern extent (Madr, Kahmard) and the Tang 悉蜜言城 = Samingan. Supports the study's one-polity reading; the capital (Sandaran or Haibak) stays open.

author: Miyamoto
asr_identification: Gūzgān, centre at Sar-i Pul = Islamic Anbīr = Bactrian Amber, the Tang 遏蜜城 where 奇沙州都督府 was set
evidence: Xin Tangshu: 奇沙州都督府 at 護時犍國遏蜜城; 遏蜜 *at-mǐět = Anbīr (Sar-i Pul); Bactrian doc. Ss dated 698 'written here at Amber'; coins of Amber; Ḥudūd: Anbīr the qasaba of Gūzgān
quote: この地域の中心地は，山脈東部に発するサフィード川が標高 600 m ほどまで下り，東側から流れてくる支流と合流する地点に位置する現在のサレ・プル，すなわちイスラーム時代の資料に見える Anbīr で…奇沙州都督府が置かれた遏蜜城である。遏蜜 (*at-mǐět) は，イスラーム時代の資料に見える Anbīr (現サレ・プル) に当たると言われており
note: Adds: the notes leave the capital of 胡寔健 unknown; the Tang commandery seat 遏蜜城 = Anbīr (if the equation holds) makes Sar-i Pul the 7th-century seat of Gūzgān, which fits Mizutani's 'Anbār?'. Not site evidence (no excavation); the equation 遏蜜 = Anbīr is reported, not argued.

author: Miyamoto
asr_identification: unidentified
evidence: None
quote: (縛喝国) の西南にあると記される最初の国 (銳秣陀国) は未比定である。
note: Agrees with the study's 'open' and, by placing Gūzgān's centre at Sar-i Pul (row :3), adds to the case against Mizutani's Sar-i-pul for 鋭秣陀.

author: Miyamoto
asr_identification: Kadagstan centred in the Baghlān–Ghōrī plain (Grenet), 活路 perhaps the unexcavated town site Qal'a-ye Ghūrī S of Surkh Kotal; Miyamoto widens Kadagstan to the Surkhāb basin, its centre perhaps shifting N-S over time
evidence: Bactrian docs T and X (commander of Kadagstan, lord of Warlugan/Wargun); Yoshida's Warlu = 活路; Grenet 2002, 2006; doc. F 'town of Lan … court of the kadag-bid' (Lan = Tang 蘭, perhaps in the Kunduz plain)
quote: Grenet は，かつて桑山說を參照し，さらに考古學2知見を考慮に入れ，この活路が，クシャーン…の神殿スルフ・コタルの南に存在するカライェ・グーリーQalʻa-ye Ghūrī という未發掘の都城跡にあたるのではないかと推測していた…その中心地が時代每にスルハーブ液域で南北に移っていたのかもしれない。
note: The notes (01.29) have Warlu/活路 in the Baghlān–Ghōrī plain; Grenet's Qal'a-ye Ghūrī and Miyamoto's wider Kadagstan are new. Bears on 縛伽浪's district, not its name; Mizutani's Baghlān stands.

author: Miyamoto
asr_identification: Qal'a-ye Zāl (reporting Kuwayama 1990), with de la Vaissière's objection to the related Hyecho 縛底耶
evidence: Kuwayama 1990 equates 遏換/阿緩, the Sui 吐火羅 capital, Xuanzang's 活國 capital and Hyecho's 縛底耶 with Qal'a-ye Zāl; de la Vaissière 2010 rejects this for 縛底耶 (Hyecho's travel days would put it W of Merv) and keeps Balkh; Miyamoto notes the objection leaves the Ghazni-Bamiyan figures unexplained
quote: は，Aてカライェ・ザールに比定される［桑山 1990：399-411］…しかし，de la Vaissière は，a超が¡底耶〜蒱特山 (バダフシャーン) 閒の旅…この記述をそのまま信用すると，¡底耶の位置をメルヴ Merv よりも西方に求めなければならなくなるとして桑山說を
note: The notes do not mention de la Vaissière's objection. It concerns Hyecho's capital, not the Life's 都城在河南岸, so it does not weaken the study's Qal'a-ye Zāl working point for 活, but it shows Kuwayama's chain of equations is contested.

author: Miyamoto
name_in_asr: 二十七国; 紇露悉泯健国
asr_identification: the 27 君長 of Tokhara = the Bactrian khar; one khar's domain = one 'country'; 紇露悉泯健 = the domain of the khar of Rob
evidence: Bactrian documents (khar of Rob; Samingan as an ōdago under him, docs N, P, Q)
quote: この「君長」に当たるのが，バクトリア語文書中で khar と呼ば…ローブ（紇露）とサミンガーン（悉泯健）を指すと考えられており，この国の範囲はローブの khar の統治圏と重なる
note: Repeats Miyamoto 2015 (row miyamoto2015:2) in summary; nothing new for location.

author: Miyamoto
asr_identification: Kadagstan centred on the Baghlān plain
evidence: Yoshida's Warlu = 活路
quote: カダグスターンの場所がバグラーン平原に特定されたのは，これ同時に言及される Warlu
note: Background only (status of the kadag-bid, the word παροαναγο); repeats 2012; adds nothing on any Xiyu ji place.

author: Iwai
name_in_asr: トハーリスターン (覩貨邏)
asr_identification: Tokharistan on both banks of the Amu, as the Chinese sources (Xuanzang) have it; the Islamic south-bank Tokharistan reflects a 7th-8th c. split
evidence: Pottery sequence (PK I-IV): bottles and large jars change in step N and S of the Amu (Chaqalak Tepe middle-upper levels; Dalverzin Tepa town and citadel), so one area from the late 3rd c.; from the 7th c. cup-shaped vessels, spouted jugs and ossuaries of Sogdian type only N (Dalverzin citadel, Zar Tepa, Kuyov Kurgan)
quote: 南北のトハーリスターンで土器の変化の流れが共通しており，アム川の南北が一体であったことが確認できるのである。…7世紀から8世紀のトハーリスターンでは，アム川の南北で生活文化に違いが現れており，7世紀後半以降にはじめてトハーリスターンに進出したムスリムたちは
note: New archaeological support, not in the notes, for Xuanzang's two-bank 覩貨邏 (Mizutani's extent). Iwai also notes that Xuanzang's return went from the Hindu Kush straight into 安呾羅縛 without Balkh (n. 17), consistent with the study's route.
